theory.intro: When two angles sit side by side and together form a right angle, they add to $90^{\circ}$. They are called **complementary** angles.
facts: If one angle is known, subtract from $90^{\circ}$ to find the other.
steps: Check the diagram shows a right angle (the two angles fill a square corner).

workedExamples.solution_text:
Angles forming a right angle add to $90^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}34^{\circ}+x&=90^{\circ}\\x&=90^{\circ}-34^{\circ}\\x&=56^{\circ}\end{align*}$

The two angles are complementary, so they add to $90^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}52^{\circ}+b&=90^{\circ}\\b&=90^{\circ}-52^{\circ}\\b&=38^{\circ}\end{align*}$
